# Tortoise & Hare

In this comic, we will depict an new app that the tortoise could have used to be awoken when there was still enough time to win the race, based on geolocation of the two contestants and their observed pace.

# Technology
The solution is a wearable/watch app. It will know the participant is in a race, and will already know all the other participants. The system knows both position (at least progress through the course), maximal pace observed, average rate so far, and estimated finishing times if either current-average is sustained or if the max is achieved from now til finish. All of this for each participant. There is a feature to be alerted if the condition arises whereby immediately accelerating to max pace will yield a win while remaining slower than max pace will allow another participant to win instead.

# characters

## Tortoise
The wise, the modest, the timeless... The tortoise almost doesn't realize he's entered a race - just moving forward at a steady slow pace and enjoys being social with his fellow community members. Will not be bothered win or lose, but will try to be a good participant.

## The Hare
A clever, very fit & fast, but ultimately lazy & complacent rabbit. Motivated to win, but only because his entire identity is comprised of believing himself obviously superior to all others, and losing just doens't fit with such beliefs. Since he is SO much better than everyone else, he also takes pride in demonstrating just how superior he is by flaunting how lazy he can be while still preserving the social rank. However, this clever Hare has hear the old tale and knows that falling asleep carries risks of social embarrasment! What to do!??

# Story
Our story diverges from the original because the Hare has a fancy new watch with a new tech device: The Keeper-Asleeper Racer-Pacer 5000. It's like an Apple Watch with a dedicate app that combines fitness tracking, race observing, and alarmclock.

The story is just like the classic, but we see the hare speak into the watch just before sitting down: "Wake me up when I can still win this race!". And of course, we see later that the tortoise does pass the hare, who remains asleep. Only when the tortoise begins to approach the finish, we see the hare's watch buzz and he springs into action! Off he sprints toward the finish with plenty of time. 

Of course, fates are not so easily changed. 
The watch gets a push notification with an advertisement for new hare-sneakers. While distracted trying to dismiss this ad, the tortoise wins!

# Structure
The entire comic should be as short as practical (about 1 page) with basic setup, a small intro to the fact that the hare has this technology, the race starting, the hare initiating the nap, the tortoise taking the lead while the hare continues to nap, the alarm, the sprint, the ad, the tortoise winning. these are the "beats".

# Scene & vibe
The scene is standard fare for the classic story. Racing from bush to tree or similar meadow/natural surroundings. There are onlookers to make the hare maximally socially-motivated. The style is casual and fun.
